# moddotplot-interactive v0.8.4

**Note:** This file was generated by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol under the direction of Adam Phillippy.

v0.8.4 gives every multi-sequence grid preview one genomic coordinate scale based on
the longest selected record. Shorter records retain their true proportional extent
instead of being stretched to fill a cell, so self and pairwise plots now line up across
the complete grid. The release remains a functional preview, and this presentation
change does not alter the estimator or the numeric contents of generated matrix cells.

See the [validation record](v0.8.4/VALIDATION.md) for completed checks and the remaining
repository-level finalization note.

## Shared genomic grid scale

Let `Lmax` be the length of the longest sequence selected for the grid. Every preview
cell now displays the common square domain `[0, Lmax] × [0, Lmax]`, regardless of which
two records it contains. The longest sequence therefore spans the complete grid width
or height wherever it appears.

For a cell with sequence `X` on the column axis and sequence `Y` on the row axis, the
supported data footprint is `[0, length(X)] × [0, length(Y)]`. A shorter self plot
occupies the lower-left fraction `length(sequence) / Lmax` on both axes, leaving the
remaining top and right portions blank. A pairwise plot independently uses the X
record's proportional width and the Y record's proportional height.

The reciprocal cell remains the true transpose of its paired preview. Its proportional
footprint is transposed with its data, preserving the established rule that the column
record is X and the row record is Y. Because every row and column uses the same genomic
units, pairwise features now align with the corresponding self plots without visually
inflating shorter chromosomes or contigs.

## Interactive comparisons

The shared scale applies to the bounded overview grid. Opening a cell still enters the
ordinary full interactive self or pairwise plot for those selected axes, with its zoom,
hover, feature-track, and export behavior unchanged. **Back to grid** returns to the
retained, proportionally scaled overview.
